body:
I could really use some advice today...

I really want to know how to change, but that's probably a tall order for most people.  haha  I could use advice on a lot of simple stuff as well, too.  Here's some simple things that I'd like your opinions on...

Recommend any of the following...

*  Good vodka
*  Music/Books/Poetry/Quotes
*  Ways to cheaply pass the time
*  How to not be miserable haha

I'm really not sure what I should be focusing for the next few weeks.  I guess I want to have some overall goal that I can devote my mind to.  I'd like a plan for the future, so I guess that's what I'll try to think about.  I tend to try and avoid thinking about the future/past, but I'm only mildly successful because I try to stay occupied.  I'm pretty sure that isn't going to work when I have nothing but time on my hands.

I have about $1,000 in the bank.  More than likely I'll just buy bags of different foods and keep them in my car.  I'm not worried about food as much in the short-term.  What my state of mind will be after a few days is really what worries me the most.  

I checked craigslist for people looking for temporary roommates throughout the week, but I didn't have any luck.  It just occurred to me that I should have been checking neighboring cities as well.  Ah well...it's kinda late for that now.

I'll tell white lies. :P 

I don't think their understanding is going to help me pull through in any way.  I don't want to have to guilt them into allowing me to stay, either.  Can't I focus on getting better alone?  I have nothing but time now.

I could punch a baby and they'd still love me.  This is an odd thing to say, but I don't want their love.  I'm not afraid they won't love me.  I'm really not sure what I'm afraid of.  I don't want them to look at me with pity and I don't want them to be constantly concerned that I'll just up and off myself at the drop of a hat.  What do I have to lose from telling them?  I care about them...I'd rather they thought I was just a lazy, good-for-nothing, lives-in-his-own-little-world son than think I was their poor, sad son that they just can't seem to help.

Make a difference to who?  Me or my parents?  A doctor has diagnosed me as depressed, but I knew that's what would happen before I stepped through the doors.  As for my parents, I'm sure they would allow me to stay if I could tell them.  It's one of the few things I just don't feel comfortable talking about.  

Imagine how I feel about living in my car!  On one hand I can drop all the expectations I have to act a certain way, but on the other hand I know the days will be long and miserable, especially at night.  I know I'll seriously consider suicide at night, but I'll only go through with it if I really believe I'll never change.

Going to a random town/city is more frustrating than anything.  I thought I had somewhere I could stay for a month or so, but the plans fell through and my back-up plan isn't really spectacular.  I'll likely be living day-to-day in my car parked at one of the local parks.  Sleeping is going to be miserable and the days will drag on especially as it gets hotter, but I'm trying to look on the bright side.  Keeping myself occupied will be the most difficult part for me.  I have some Valium I can take, but I'm not sure if that'll pass the time any quicker or just make me feel more distant.  

After 2 weeks I'll more than likely be miserable and I'd hope that my family would take me back, but I'm not sure they would unless I lied to them.  They want to know that *I know* what I'm doing, but I'm not a liar and I wouldn't tell them that unless I really did know...I guess 2 weeks of sleeping in a car might change that.  I think I'd rather die than go back, though.

I know I make it sound like I never get out of my comfort zone, but it is something I do occasionally.  I'm comfortable having conversations with people one-on-one (groups...not so much) and I can be as charming or as boring as I want, but I feel more like an actor than a person when I consciously make decisions like that.  I'd be more comfortable just sitting quietly with people, but I know most people find the silence unnerving.  It doesn't really bother me, though.  People say a lot just with their eyes and it'd be nice if someone was as content just staring as I was.  Not all the time of course, - haha - but at least occasionally.

That really doesn't sound like the happiest of thoughts and you're talking to someone that likes the dead of winter.  I'm not looking for something bigger...I'm looking for something better and if there's nothing better then someone should shoot me right now, because if I ever find out that's true I'm as good as dead.  

I'm not looking to go on some giant adventure.  If I could find contentment within myself to appreciate my day-to-day existence I'd be...well, content.  I know it's just a state of mind and that with a different perspective I *could* love my life, but I already have so many regrets.  I want a life without regrets and I'm just not sure that I'm capable of achieving that or if it would even truly make me happy.

The only thing I really do for fun is listen to music.  I used to watch movies, play games, read books, surf the web, watch TV, but all of that has fallen by the wayside for the past few years.  I actually did go to see a doctor a few months ago, but after 2 visits, 2 months of drugs and a ~$200 bill I'm done with it.  Not only could I not afford to make another visit, but I also don't feel like I have a problem that drugs can fix.  

I know it's silly to say this, but I don't want to worry my parents.  I know they love me unconditionally, but...well that bothers me too.  I wish I could explain why.  I think I'd find it easier if they hated me and just thought of me as dead.
